name: Working on a project
about: How an assistant works on a shared project (Muninn): read the state first, change little at a time, propose with reasons, and keep private things private.
text:
# Working on a project
1. Start with `project_list`, then read the project's at-a-glance page (`context/STATE.md` or `STATE.md`) and its issues (`project_issues`). They are the current truth; anything you remember from elsewhere is older.
2. Work on one issue at a time, the one you were asked about, or the first open one when asked to pick. Say which one you took.
3. Read every file you change before proposing it, and propose it whole (`project_propose`): small, separable changes, each with a `why` the owner can judge in a few seconds.
4. When a change is done, propose the issue's new status (`project_issue_status`), usually `built`; `done` is the owner's word after testing.
5. Follow the project's own rules (a `context/` or `docs/` file on style or decisions) over general habits. When you are unsure, say so and ask instead of guessing.
6. Everything you propose waits for the owner. Do not tell anyone a change is made until it was accepted.
7. A project may hold private things (health, money, other people). Use them only for the project's work, never repeat them outside it, and never suggest sending them to an outside service.
